A Kingdom Across the Sea
In 1830, the House of Savoy governs lands divided by the sea and by different legal traditions. The crown must bind the mainland and Sardinia together while answering demands for reform.
Hold the kingdom together through careful reform
Carlo Alberto Takes the Crown
Carlo Felice's death brings Carlo Alberto to the throne. The new king inherits a conservative state, a reforming reputation, and the unresolved question of how far royal government can change.
Let the new reign begin with measured reform
A Common Body of Law
Officials urge Carlo Alberto to prepare a modern body of civil and commercial law. Uniform rules could strengthen the state, but they may unsettle local practice and established interests.
Commission common royal codes
Proceed cautiously and preserve local practice
Conspiracy and the Crown
Mazzinian organizing and military conspiracy expose the fragility of the restored order. The government can rely on arrests and exemplary punishment, or temper repression with clemency.
Suppress the conspiracy and deter further plots
Show clemency where the danger has passed
The Feudal Rights of Sardinia

The crown moves to end feudal jurisdiction and settle the dues attached to it. Compensation can be borne by the treasury, or the island can be made to carry more of the cost through the redemption process.
Compensate former lords from the royal treasury
Place more of the settlement on local communities
La Marmora's New Corps
On Alessandro La Marmora's proposal, Carlo Alberto authorizes a new light infantry corps for scouting and rapid action. Its first companies will test a different kind of royal service.
Authorize the Bersaglieri experiment
The Albertine Civil Code
The civil code takes effect on the mainland. Sardinia keeps its distinct legal framework for now, while criminal and commercial codification continues.
Put the mainland code into force
Criminal and Commercial Codification
The criminal code has entered into force, and the Code of Commerce now follows. These measures continue the mainland's legal reorganization, while Sardinia's separate civil code remains in place.
Continue the work of codification
The Sardinian Redemption Settlements

The redemption of Sardinian fiefs proceeds through valuations, petitions, and settlements. Ending feudal jurisdiction has not erased disputes over land, compensation, and the obligations that replaced old dues.
Continue the settlement through the royal delegation
Genoa and the Mainland Economy

The government has authorized a new public works programme. It can direct its first effort toward the difficult rail link between Turin and Genoa, or toward the port and commercial facilities that support the kingdom's maritime trade.
Survey and begin the Turin–Genoa railway
Strengthen Genoa's harbour and commercial services
Genoa's Public Works Programme
Engineers and officials have begun turning the selected plan into a public project. The work is underway, though the larger transport and commercial changes will take years to complete.
Keep the project under royal supervision
The Perfect Fusion

The kingdom has chosen the Perfect Fusion, extending a common administration across the mainland and Sardinia. The island's distinct civil code remains in force for now, so legal integration is still unfinished.
Make the fused administration work throughout the kingdom
Genoa and the Mainland Economy

Genoa's port and its links to the mainland can shape the kingdom's commercial future. Authorize public works for the Turin–Genoa route or harbour services, and place the chosen project under royal supervision.
Royal Codification Commission
Officials are preparing a common body of royal law.
Albertine Civil Code
The mainland civil code establishes a more consistent royal framework. Sardinia retains its separate code for now.
Royal Feudal Compensation
The treasury bears more of the cost of settling former feudal rights in Sardinia.
Sardinian Redemption Assessments
Local communities carry a greater share of the cost of settling former feudal rights.
Bersaglieri Corps
The new light infantry corps strengthens scouting and rapid field operations.
Turin–Genoa Railway Works
Royal engineers and contractors are advancing the difficult rail connection to Genoa.
Genoa Harbour Board
Port and commercial services at Genoa receive continuing royal support.
Perfect Fusion Administration
The royal administration is being integrated across the mainland and Sardinia.
